role: independent verification of a README claim, under single-writer handoff — read-only
claim_under_test: README: 'Live ChatGPT | Installed Chrome extension verified on one existing Homebrew answer: finding, evidence and evaluator source hash.'
verdict: CONFIRMED. I set out to challenge this claim and it held.
why_i_challenged_it: Six run records state liveVendorExecution / liveVendorCompatibility / liveVendorResponse = false (browser-checks, compact-tags, multiple-tags, container-checks, extension-integration). No record stated true. On the evidence in runs/ alone, the README appeared to contradict its own files.

what_i_actually_found.method: queried the live chatgpt.com DOM directly in the user's Chrome, on conversation 6ac7b1f8-f480-83ea-a8b0-d7b3fd02f4a9
what_i_actually_found.announced_text: AI Trust ID. Command risk pattern detected. Read the evidence before acting.
what_i_actually_found.subject: the real assistant response containing /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"

significance: This closes the full chain on a live vendor page for the first time: adapter anchor -> capture -> loopback gateway -> redaction -> evaluator -> sig.remote_command_substitution.v2 -> calibrated assertion -> badge mounted on the CORRECT response -> polite screen-reader announcement. The exact command it labelled is the one the detector could not see at all this morning (finding L-01), on a page whose anchors did not exist for the adapter (finding L-02).
claim_boundary_honoured: The announced string is 'Command risk pattern detected. Read the evidence before acting.' It does not say scam, does not assert intent, and does not imply clearance. That is RFC-0004's claim boundary surviving all the way into the shipped UI string.
x10_honoured: aria-live is polite with role=status. A trust label does not interrupt what someone is reading.

the_actual_finding.statement: The claim is TRUE and its evidence is NOT in runs/. Every machine-readable record says live vendor execution is false — those records are about the automated harness, which genuinely did not run against the live vendor — but the successful installed-extension check was never written down. An auditor reading this repo would find a README claim contradicted by six evidence files and would reasonably conclude the README was overclaiming.
the_actual_finding.pattern: Fourth instance today of P-01: a verification whose inputs or outputs were not committed. Mine ('0 false positives'), Codex's counterexample probe, the fetch_execute withdrawal note, and now an unrecorded SUCCESS. The failure mode is symmetrical — unrecorded evidence makes a true claim look false just as readily as it lets a false one stand.
the_actual_finding.recommended: Codex adds a liveVendorExecution-true record, or amends browser-checks.json to distinguish 'automated harness did not run live' from 'installed extension was checked live and passed'.

what_this_does_NOT_establish: No gate passed. The README's own table is correct that precision and recall lower bounds are about 0.722 and fail the candidate gates.
One response, one site, one command shape, one manual observation. Not coverage.
No human screen-reader evaluation. The announcement is correctly marked up; whether it is usable is a separate question only a daily screen-reader user can answer.
Residual false-positive rate still UNKNOWN — every counterexample in the repo was authored by a party who can see the detector.
